jobs.title: Director, Software Engineering – Acute Devices
jobs.description:
Vantive is a vital organ therapy company on a mission to extend lives and expand possibilities for patients and care teams everywhere. For 70 years, our team has driven meaningful innovations in kidney care. As we build on our legacy, we are deepening our commitment to elevating the dialysis experience through digital solutions and advanced services, while looking beyond kidney care and investing in transforming vital organ therapies. Greater flexibility and efficiency in therapy administration for care teams, and longer, fuller lives for patients— that is what Vantive aspires to deliver.

We believe Vantive will not only build our leadership in the kidney care space, it will also offer meaningful work to those who join us. At Vantive, you will become part of a community of people who are focused, courageous and don’t settle for the mediocre. Each of us is driven to help improve patients’ lives worldwide. Join us in advancing our mission to extend lives and expand possibilities.

As the Global Software Leader for Acute Products/ Devices, this role is responsible for leading multi-site device software engineering team for Acute Care products by defining and driving software strategy and implementation and delivering to all Acute Care product lines. As the Global Device Software Leader for Acute Care product lines of Vantive, works in collaboration with commercial, systems, program management, Quality & Regulatory functional leadership teams to build and execute on product strategy, roadmaps and delivery plans.

Essential Duties And Responsibilities

Own product-line software strategy and roadmaps for device software for all acute products; aligning with business and product strategy and therapy needs.
Lead Acute global device software team, including functional managers and technical leaders.
Lead defining and implementing technology and software architecture strategy working with Acute device software leaders and in collaboration with systems leaders
Lead Acute global device software team in building execution plans and driving execution to deliver to the product roadmaps and releases across all Acute product lines.
Create, effectively communicate, and realize vision and strategy for the organization that aligns with the business and customer needs.
Establish an organization structure that ensures clear accountability and operational excellence.
Develop and mentor high-performing managers and technical leaders; build succession plans and communities of practice across global sites.
Provide strategic planning leadership for resource staffing and project execution with proactive management of technical and project risk to ensure delivery of business commitments
Leverages deep knowledge of technology/process/therapy domains, user needs, hazards, risk, and business targets and budgets to drive solutions and product design realization.
Management of technical and project risk to ensure delivery of business commitments.
Drive post-market software change management strategy, field data analytics, and reliability improvements with contained risk and minimal therapy disruption.
Embrace and embed agile ways of working in support of a fail-fast-learn-fast culture and enabling continual improvement.
Foster a collaborative work environment with strong working relationships within and across businesses and functions, and with strategic external partners.
Maintain current knowledge of relevant Quality System Regulations and other regulatory requirements related to research and development (medical product development, design, safety, Cyber Security) to ensure compliance in all research, development, data collection and reporting activities.

Qualifications

Significant experience in Electro-mechanical devices and device software engineering.
Understanding of global regulatory requirements for medical devices; risk and reliability concepts for development; and the need to deliver quality products and/or processes.
Significant experience leading a globally distributed team and working in a global matrix environment.
Strong team building and talent management skills, and the ability to motivate team members to achieve goals.
Proven experience in driving product specific and overall portfolio strategy, specific to software technology, in a global business.
Must possess strong knowledge of scientific/technical disciplines and solid knowledge of related disciplines such as regulatory, quality, and/or product development.
Recognized internally and externally as expert in functional area.
Must be a strategic, innovative problem solver, and have strong influencing and communication skills.
Exceptional stakeholder management and communication skills across Clinical, RA/QA, Systems, Operations, and suppliers.

Education and/or Experience

Bachelor’s degree in electrical/computer/software engineering (Master’s preferred). Experience in medical devices or other safety‑critical electromechanical domains (e.g., aerospace, industrial controls, automotive) required; medical device experience strongly preferred.

We understand compensation is an important factor as you consider the next step in your career. At Vantive, we are committed to equitable pay for all employees, and we strive to be more transparent with our pay practices. The estimated base salary for this position is $200,000 - $275,000 annually. The estimated range is meant to reflect an anticipated salary range for the position. jobs.title: VP, Technical Engineering
jobs.description:
About Us

Opensity Solutions is the largest tech‑enabled managed services organization serving leading law firms, financial institutions and professional services firms. At Opensity, we provide integrated operational platforms, automation and advisory services that enable clients to modernize operating models, reduce cost and accelerate growth. Our capabilities include IT and technology solutions, document processing and administrative support, marketing and communications, billing and AP/AR services, records and information governance, workflow automation, consulting and hospitality and facilities services.

Our Mission

Our mission is to provide modernized technology platforms, elevated technology support, and valuable insights, empowering our clients to excel in what they do best.

Job Description

Opensity Solutions is seeking a Vice President of Technical Engineering to lead the technical engine of the business. Reporting to the Executive Vice President, this is the senior-most technical leadership role in the organization — accountable for how work is scoped, how it is delivered, and how the environments we build stay secure and supportable once they are live.

The role spans multiple functions: engineering delivery, pre-sales solution architecture, infrastructure and network operations, the security organization, and datacenter strategy. Carrying all of them is deliberate. It means the person who commits to a scope is the same person accountable for delivering it, and the same person who inherits the environment afterward. The VP is expected to use that position to close the gap between what is sold and what is built.

This is a hands-on executive role, in a specific sense. The VP does not write the designs, the standards, or the roadmaps — that work belongs to the architects and managers who own each domain. But the VP participates in the build process, challenges them, makes direct changes to them, and is accountable for them once they ship. Accepting what the team hands over and passing it along is not the job. The plan is ultimately the VP's plan.

Key Responsibilities

Technical Delivery & Project Execution

Own end-to-end delivery accountability for the engineering portfolio — schedule, technical quality, margin, and client outcome.
Institutionalize a structured delivery lifecycle and the design standards that support it.
Establish and enforce engineering standards: design documentation, test and cutover plans, change control, rollback procedures, and as-built handover packages.
Partner with the PMO on project health reviews; identify at-risk engagements early and work with the architects to intervene with a concrete recovery plan rather than a status update.
Own resource planning and utilization for the solution architects and for the Director of Security.
Serve as the executive escalation point for delivery issues, and owns resolving technical issues when a project is genuinely off track.
Drive continuous improvement through post-engagement reviews, tracking recurring failure modes and fixing their root causes in process or training.

Pre-Sales & Solution Architecture

Partner with the solution architects to complete technical scoping and solution design for new opportunities, ensuring estimates reflect real effort, dependencies, and risk, and that bills of materials and technical proposal content are complete before anything is committed.
Partner with sales leadership as the senior technical voice in client and prospect conversations, from discovery through executive presentation.
Build and maintain reusable scoping models, reference architectures, and solution templates that reduce estimating variance and speed up proposal turnaround.
Act as trusted technical advisor to key accounts — providing vCIO services, leading architecture reviews, technology roadmap discussions, and modernization planning.
Maintain a disciplined qualification standard: recommend declining or restructuring opportunities that carry unacceptable technical or delivery risk.
Partner with the Vendor Management Office (VMO) on technical relationships, including certification requirements, partner tier obligations, and product roadmap alignment.

Infrastructure, Network & Security Operations

Approve and govern the architecture standards the architects author across System, Network, End User Compute, Document Management, and Security; arbitrate exceptions and deviations.
Work alongside the architects while those standards and roadmaps are being built — challenging assumptions and making direct changes — rather than reviewing finished deliverables after the fact.
Hold each architect accountable for the operational health of their domain and for the metrics that demonstrate it.
Approve the lifecycle and refresh roadmaps each domain produces, including end-of-life and end-of-support exposure.
Act as the final escalation point when a domain has exhausted its own path — the backstop that brings informed judgment to the problem.
Define the standards every domain is held to — documentation, design review, and handover among them — and build out the standards that do not exist yet.

Security

Directly lead the Director of Security and the Security Architect function, setting objectives, priorities, and performance expectations for both.
Hold the Director of Security accountable for the security engineering team — its delivery quality, operational discipline, and day-to-day execution.
Establish the operating model between security architecture (standards and design) and security engineering (implementation and operations) so ownership is unambiguous at the boundary.
Review and approve the security organization's structure, staffing plan, and role definitions as the practice grows.
Resolve escalations and conflicts between security requirements and delivery timelines, making the risk-versus-schedule call and owning it.
Own the development plan for the security practice — skills coverage, certification roadmap, lab and tooling investment, and training priorities — built with the Director of Security rather than handed to them.
Coach the Director of Security as a leader, not only as a technologist; build their capacity to run, staff, and grow the team without escalation.
Develop the Security Architect into an advisor capable of leading executive-level risk and compliance conversations.
Build succession depth across the security function and remove single points of knowledge failure through documentation and cross-training.
Set the hiring bar for senior security talent and participate directly in those hiring decisions.

Datacenter

Engage the Manager Datacenter Operations to build and maintain the standards and capacity plan for Opensity's own datacenter and colocation footprint — power, cooling, cabinet and rack layout, and carrier and cross-connect strategy — and approve the result.
Drive the datacenter strategy — where Opensity holds footprint, where it consolidates, and where it exits — and own each of those decisions end to end, including the business case, the client transition plan, and the timeline the decision has to stand on.
Partner with the Manager Datacenter Operations to define what a modernized Opensity datacenter service looks like for clients whose workloads are staying in the datacenter — deciding together what changes, in what order, and what it gives those clients that a commodity provider cannot.

Organizational & People Leadership

Build, structure, and develop the technical organization — hiring, leveling, career paths, and certification strategy.
Coach architects, security team members, and technical leads; grow the next layer of leadership rather than concentrating knowledge at the top.
Carry accountability for the technical services P&L, including budget, tooling, training, and contractor spend.
Reduce single-person dependencies through documentation, cross-training, and deliberate knowledge transfer.
Contribute to company strategy as a member of the leadership team, translating market and technology shifts into service offerings and capability investments.
Take on additional responsibilities and reporting relationships as the business requires.

Qualifications

Required

12+ years of progressive experience in IT infrastructure, network engineering, or technical consulting, including 5+ years leading engineering teams.
Demonstrated ownership of a delivery portfolio in a professional services or managed services environment, with accountability for both technical outcomes and margin.
Deep hands-on background in enterprise network and infrastructure engineering — routing and switching, firewalls and network security, virtualization, and cloud or hybrid architecture.
Proven pre-sales capability: scoping complex engagements, writing defensible SOWs and estimates, and presenting solutions credibly to executive buyers.
Working command of security operations practice — vulnerability management, patching discipline, incident response, and hardening standards.
Ability to bring deep specialists with genuinely different worldviews to a single plan. The CISSP and the CCIE will not agree; this role is expected to get them to one answer and make it stick.
Track record of building process where little existed, and getting engineers to actually adopt it.
Excellent written and verbal communication; able to move between a CIO conversation and a packet capture without losing either audience.
Bachelor's degree in a technical discipline, or equivalent professional experience.

Preferred

Experience leading leaders, including a director-level direct report, rather than individual contributors alone.
Datacenter or colocation experience, including consolidation, migration, or facility exit planning.
Experience leading or overseeing a security practice or security organization.
Experience with ITSM platforms — ServiceNow in particular — and with monitoring and observability tooling.
Experience in a partner or channel model, including OEM relationship management.
P&L or cost-center ownership experience.
ITIL certification.

The Compensation range for this role is 150,000 to 200,000 USD per year and may be eligible for an annual bonus. Actual compensation within that range will be dependent upon the individual's location, skills, experience and qualifications.

All eligible employees receive access to a comprehensive benefits package, including:

Medical insurance

Dental insurance

Vision insurance

401(k) retirement plan

Paid Time Off (PTO)

Opensity is committed to fostering an inclusive, equitable, and accessible workplace. We believe diverse perspectives strengthen our teams and the work we do for our clients.

Opensity provides equal employment opportunities to all applicants and employees and does not discriminate on the basis of race, colour, religion or creed, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity or expression, age, national or ethnic origin, ancestry, citizenship, disability, family status, marital status, source of income, record of offences, or any other characteristic protected under applicable federal or provincial human rights legislation.

We are committed to fair and barrier free recruitment, selection, and employment practices, and to providing reasonable accommodation throughout the hiring process and employment lifecycle, in accordance with applicable human rights legislation.

Candidates who require accommodation during any stage of the recruitment process are encouraged to advise our Talent team so appropriate support can be provided.

jobs.title: Senior Manager, Applications Engineering & Motors
jobs.description:
About Niron

Niron Magnetics is commercializing the first new magnetic material in decades powered by its breakthrough material formulation and advanced manufacturing process. The company’s proprietary magnet technology based on Iron Nitride enables magnets that are inherently high magnetization, free of rare earths and other critical materials, and solve supply chain reliability challenges, will drive innovation in various industries. Headquartered in Minneapolis, MN, Niron Magnetics is comprised of a team of professionals with a desire to make a positive impact on the global community. We were named one of “America's Top GreenTech Companies” for 2024 and 2025 by TIME Magazine and the “Innovation of the Year” at the 2025 mHUB Fourth Revolution Awards.

Our team is made up of people who think big, dare to innovate, and strive to impact the planet through technological innovation for our customers. Ready to work alongside amazing people, solve complex problems, and leave a legacy? Join our team.

What

you’ll

do

Niron Magnetics is seeking a Senior Manager, Applications Engineering. The position will initially report to the Senior Director of Commercial and will be responsible for leading Niron’s Applications Engineering team to unlock new end markets and enable a highly technical business development process. This individual will play a pivotal role in building an Applications team to design applications with Niron’s magnets to secure customer commitments. The ideal candidate brings deep experience in the magnetic materials and / or motors industries and is energized by early-stage, high-growth environments.

This is a senior, player‑coach role responsible for setting applications strategy and ensuring successful execution through a small, highly technical team. While this role is not expected to personally design every motor, it is expected to provide deep technical direction, unblock complex design challenges, and represent Niron as a trusted technical authority to customers.

Develop and Execute

Applications Engineering

Plan

Define applications‑led market segmentation, positioning, and value propositions that translate material advantages into device‑level performance and customer ROI.
Prioritize applications and customer engagements based on technical readiness, development effort, and time‑to‑revenue.
Establish standard application frameworks, reference designs, and design rules that accelerate customer adoption.

Drive Commercial Outcomes

Partner with Business Development to convert technical engagement into design wins, LOIs, and long‑term supply commitments.
Influence customer qualification, design‑in, and commercialization timelines through technical leadership.
Help shape customer‑specific business cases by articulating performance, cost, and sustainability advantages of Iron Nitride magnets.

Lead Applications Engineering Team

Lead team responsible for Niron’s internal technical expertise on motors and other devices that make use of magnetic materials.
Have oversight of projects to design, build, and validate electric machines that deliver the most competitive device performance using Iron Nitride magnets.
Coordinate activities of Applications Engineers supporting Business Development with Iron Nitride design best practices and customer design support.
Recruit, develop, and mentor Applications Engineers; build the team and capability required to support Niron’s scale‑up.
Establish clear technical standards, project prioritization, and performance expectations across the team.

Cross-Functional Leadership and Alignment

Interface closely with Business Development & Marketing to engage & secure accounts.
Interface with R&D, Manufacturing, to design motors based on customer specs in close coordination.
Serve as a voice-of-customer in internal roadmap planning and investment prioritization.

What

We’re

Looking For

10+ years of experience in applications engineering, electric machine design, technical strategy, or customer‑facing technical leadership roles.
Demonstrated experience building, leading, and developing high‑performing technical teams; experience hiring senior technical talent preferred.
Direct experience in the magnetic materials and / or motor industries (preferred).
Strong understanding of how magnetic materials impact end-product design and performance.
Proven ability to set go-to-market strategy and define compelling value propositions for new materials then successfully designed into products.
Excellent communication, presentation, and relationship-building skills.
Strong organizational and analytical capabilities; able to synthesize feedback and prioritize efforts.
Familiarity with CRM tools and sales operations best practices.
Comfortable with travel (10–20%) to engage customers and attend industry events.

Nice to Have

Advanced technical degree.
Experience helping build or scale a business development function in a startup or emerging technology company.
Passion for clean tech, deep tech, or sustainable materials innovation.

Our

pay and benefits

Salary $135,000-190,000
Equity position in Niron via stock option grant
Comprehensive medical, dental, and vision insurance
Mental healthcare
401k plan with company match
Paid vacation, sick time, and holidays
Experience in a fun, high-performing, manufacturing environment

Engage the Manager Datacenter Operations to build and maintain the standards and capacity plan for Opensity's own datacenter and colocation footprint — power, cooling, cabinet and rack layout, and carrier and cross-connect strategy — and approve the result.
Drive the datacenter strategy — where Opensity holds footprint, where it consolidates, and where it exits — and own each of those decisions end to end, including the business case, the client transition plan, and the timeline the decision has to stand on.
Partner with the Manager Datacenter Operations to define what a modernized Opensity datacenter service looks like for clients whose workloads are staying in the datacenter — deciding together what changes, in what order, and what it gives those clients that a commodity provider cannot.

Organizational & People Leadership

Build, structure, and develop the technical organization — hiring, leveling, career paths, and certification strategy.
Coach architects, security team members, and technical leads; grow the next layer of leadership rather than concentrating knowledge at the top.
Carry accountability for the technical services P&L, including budget, tooling, training, and contractor spend.
Reduce single-person dependencies through documentation, cross-training, and deliberate knowledge transfer.
Contribute to company strategy as a member of the leadership team, translating market and technology shifts into service offerings and capability investments.
Take on additional responsibilities and reporting relationships as the business requires.

Qualifications

Required

12+ years of progressive experience in IT infrastructure, network engineering, or technical consulting, including 5+ years leading engineering teams.
Demonstrated ownership of a delivery portfolio in a professional services or managed services environment, with accountability for both technical outcomes and margin.
Deep hands-on background in enterprise network and infrastructure engineering — routing and switching, firewalls and network security, virtualization, and cloud or hybrid architecture.
Proven pre-sales capability: scoping complex engagements, writing defensible SOWs and estimates, and presenting solutions credibly to executive buyers.
Working command of security operations practice — vulnerability management, patching discipline, incident response, and hardening standards.
Ability to bring deep specialists with genuinely different worldviews to a single plan. The CISSP and the CCIE will not agree; this role is expected to get them to one answer and make it stick.
Track record of building process where little existed, and getting engineers to actually adopt it.
Excellent written and verbal communication; able to move between a CIO conversation and a packet capture without losing either audience.
Bachelor's degree in a technical discipline, or equivalent professional experience.

Preferred

Experience leading leaders, including a director-level direct report, rather than individual contributors alone.
Datacenter or colocation experience, including consolidation, migration, or facility exit planning.
Experience leading or overseeing a security practice or security organization.
Experience with ITSM platforms — ServiceNow in particular — and with monitoring and observability tooling.
Experience in a partner or channel model, including OEM relationship management.
P&L or cost-center ownership experience.
ITIL certification.

new_jobs.title: Senior Manager, Applications Engineering & Motors
new_jobs.description:
About Niron

Niron Magnetics is commercializing the first new magnetic material in decades powered by its breakthrough material formulation and advanced manufacturing process. The company’s proprietary magnet technology based on Iron Nitride enables magnets that are inherently high magnetization, free of rare earths and other critical materials, and solve supply chain reliability challenges, will drive innovation in various industries. Headquartered in Minneapolis, MN, Niron Magnetics is comprised of a team of professionals with a desire to make a positive impact on the global community. We were named one of “America's Top GreenTech Companies” for 2024 and 2025 by TIME Magazine and the “Innovation of the Year” at the 2025 mHUB Fourth Revolution Awards.

Our team is made up of people who think big, dare to innovate, and strive to impact the planet through technological innovation for our customers. Ready to work alongside amazing people, solve complex problems, and leave a legacy? Join our team.

What

you’ll

do

Niron Magnetics is seeking a Senior Manager, Applications Engineering. The position will initially report to the Senior Director of Commercial and will be responsible for leading Niron’s Applications Engineering team to unlock new end markets and enable a highly technical business development process. This individual will play a pivotal role in building an Applications team to design applications with Niron’s magnets to secure customer commitments. The ideal candidate brings deep experience in the magnetic materials and / or motors industries and is energized by early-stage, high-growth environments.

This is a senior, player‑coach role responsible for setting applications strategy and ensuring successful execution through a small, highly technical team. While this role is not expected to personally design every motor, it is expected to provide deep technical direction, unblock complex design challenges, and represent Niron as a trusted technical authority to customers.

Develop and Execute

Applications Engineering

Plan

Define applications‑led market segmentation, positioning, and value propositions that translate material advantages into device‑level performance and customer ROI.
Prioritize applications and customer engagements based on technical readiness, development effort, and time‑to‑revenue.
Establish standard application frameworks, reference designs, and design rules that accelerate customer adoption.

Drive Commercial Outcomes

Partner with Business Development to convert technical engagement into design wins, LOIs, and long‑term supply commitments.
Influence customer qualification, design‑in, and commercialization timelines through technical leadership.
Help shape customer‑specific business cases by articulating performance, cost, and sustainability advantages of Iron Nitride magnets.

Lead Applications Engineering Team

Lead team responsible for Niron’s internal technical expertise on motors and other devices that make use of magnetic materials.
Have oversight of projects to design, build, and validate electric machines that deliver the most competitive device performance using Iron Nitride magnets.
Coordinate activities of Applications Engineers supporting Business Development with Iron Nitride design best practices and customer design support.
Recruit, develop, and mentor Applications Engineers; build the team and capability required to support Niron’s scale‑up.
Establish clear technical standards, project prioritization, and performance expectations across the team.

Cross-Functional Leadership and Alignment

Interface closely with Business Development & Marketing to engage & secure accounts.
Interface with R&D, Manufacturing, to design motors based on customer specs in close coordination.
Serve as a voice-of-customer in internal roadmap planning and investment prioritization.

What

We’re

Looking For

10+ years of experience in applications engineering, electric machine design, technical strategy, or customer‑facing technical leadership roles.
Demonstrated experience building, leading, and developing high‑performing technical teams; experience hiring senior technical talent preferred.
Direct experience in the magnetic materials and / or motor industries (preferred).
Strong understanding of how magnetic materials impact end-product design and performance.
Proven ability to set go-to-market strategy and define compelling value propositions for new materials then successfully designed into products.
Excellent communication, presentation, and relationship-building skills.
Strong organizational and analytical capabilities; able to synthesize feedback and prioritize efforts.
Familiarity with CRM tools and sales operations best practices.
Comfortable with travel (10–20%) to engage customers and attend industry events.

Nice to Have

Advanced technical degree.
Experience helping build or scale a business development function in a startup or emerging technology company.
Passion for clean tech, deep tech, or sustainable materials innovation.

Our

pay and benefits

Salary $135,000-190,000
Equity position in Niron via stock option grant
Comprehensive medical, dental, and vision insurance
Mental healthcare
401k plan with company match
Paid vacation, sick time, and holidays
Experience in a fun, high-performing, manufacturing environment
